## Physical AI and Embodied Systems Notation {#sec-notation-physical}

Physical AI and embodied machine learning systems merge three distinct technical traditions:

1. **Machine Learning and Deep Learning** (statistical optimization, transformers, diffusion policies, imitation learning, autoregression).
2. **Robotics, Mechanics, and Classical Control** (multibody dynamics, $SE(3)$ Lie groups, rigid-body kinematics, Lyapunov stability, Control Barrier Functions, actuator drive physics).
3. **Embedded Systems and Real-Time Architectures** (system-on-chip interconnects, cache and memory bus contention, hardware interrupt latency, intent leases, fail-safe interlocks).

Because each discipline developed its mathematical notation independently over decades, combining them creates severe symbol collisions—the "traditional warts" of cyber-physical engineering. Below, we formalize the governing laws of embodied systems, establish a cross-discipline disambiguation contract, and tabulate the canonical symbols used throughout this book.

## Cross-Discipline Disambiguation and Traditional Warts {#sec-notation-disambiguation .unlisted}

When physical plant dynamics meet deep neural networks, common mathematical shorthand breaks down. For instance, the symbol $\theta$ classically denotes a robot joint angle in kinematics, but denotes neural network weights in machine learning. Writing $\nabla_\theta \pi_\theta(\mathbf{a} \mid \mathbf{q})$ without disambiguation confuses spatial configuration with parameter gradients.

The conventions below resolve these cross-domain collisions systematically:

::: {tbl-colwidths="[12,18,18,52]"}

| **Symbol**                              | **Canonical Convention**                                                                   | **Colliding Meaning**                                                                        | **Disambiguation Rule**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
|:----------------------------------------|:-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|:---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|:----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **$\theta$**                            | Neural policy network weights $\pi_\theta$                                                 | Joint angle $\theta_i$ in kinematics                                                         | **Reserve $\theta$ strictly for neural parameters**. Joint configurations are always generalized coordinates $\mathbf{q} \in \mathbb{R}^n$ and $q_i$.                                                                                                                                               |
| **$P$**                                 | Model parameter count ($P$ or $P_{\text{params}}$)                                         | Power ($P_{\text{elec}}$), Pressure ($P_{\text{fluid}}$), or Position ($\mathbf{p}$)         | Use $P$ for parameter count (consistent with foundational ML systems conventions). Electrical/mechanical power is $P_{\text{elec}}$ or $P_{\text{mech}}$ (in Watts); fluid pressure is $P(t)$ or $p_{\text{fluid}}$ (in bar or Pa); spatial 3D translation is vector $\mathbf{p} = [x, y, z]^\top$. |
| **$\boldsymbol{\tau}$**                 | Actuator torque/force vector ($\text{N}\cdot\text{m}$ or $\text{N}$)                       | Temporal response threshold or checkpoint interval $\tau_{\text{opt}}$                       | Realized physical torque is always bold vector $\boldsymbol{\tau} \in \mathbb{R}^n$ or scalar joint torque $\tau_i$. Temporal constants and intervals use $t$, $\Delta t$, or $T$.                                                                                                                  |
| **$a$ vs. $u$ vs. $\boldsymbol{\tau}$** | Action pipeline stages ($a \to \hat{u} \to u^* \to \boldsymbol{\tau}$)                     | Single generic "action" symbol                                                               | Disambiguate execution authority: $a_t \in \mathcal{A}$ is the unprivileged policy action; $\hat{u}_t$ is the proposed plant control setpoint; $u^*_t$ is the certified, CBF-filtered control; $\boldsymbol{\tau}_t$ is the realized physical actuator torque.                                      |
| **$B$**                                 | Batch size ($B$ or $B_{\text{tokens}}$)                                                    | Bandwidth ($\text{BW}$) or Body reference frame ($\mathcal{F}_B$)                            | Batch size is $B$; bandwidth is $\text{BW}$ (per the foundational iron law); coordinate reference frames use calligraphic script ($\mathcal{F}_W$ for World, $\mathcal{F}_B$ for Body, $\mathcal{F}_E$ for End-effector).                                                                           |
| **$N$**                                 | Cluster compute node count (in distributed scaling contexts)                               | Gear reduction ratio ($N_{\text{gear}}$) or Newtons ($\text{N}$)                             | Gearbox reduction ratio is written with an explicit subscript $N_{\text{gear}} \gg 1$; physical force units are upright roman $\text{N}$; compute nodes/accelerators use $N$ or $N_{\text{dev}}$.                                                                                                   |
| **$\alpha$**                            | Bumpless transfer blend parameter $\alpha(t) \in [0, 1]$                                   | Network latency ($\alpha$ in $\alpha$-$\beta$) or angular acceleration ($\ddot{\mathbf{q}}$) | Authority blending uses scalar function $\alpha(t) \in [0, 1]$; joint angular acceleration is $\ddot{\mathbf{q}}$ ($\text{rad/s}^2$); network latency uses $L_{\text{net}}$ or context-qualified $\alpha$.                                                                                          |
| **$\mathbf{x}$ vs. $x$**                | Mechanical plant state vector $\mathbf{x} = [\mathbf{q}^\top, \dot{\mathbf{q}}^\top]^\top$ | Scalar input token or tensor $x$                                                             | Continuous physical plant state is always bold $\mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^{2n}$; token or feature inputs use plain italic $x$ or latent vector $\mathbf{z}$.                                                                                                                                        |

:::

## The Embodied Iron Law: Sense-to-Torque Latency Budget {#sec-notation-embodied-iron-law .unlisted}

In physical systems, computational latency directly translates into unmodeled plant drift and positional error. Building on the serialized execution decomposition of the iron law of ML Systems, the total closed-loop sense-to-torque loop time $T_{\text{loop}}$ must satisfy the hard real-time cadence bound:

$$T_{\text{loop}} = \underbrace{t_{\text{sense}}}_{\text{Exposure \& Readout}} + \underbrace{t_{\text{xfer}}}_{\text{DMA \& Bus Ingest}} + \underbrace{t_{\text{infer}}}_{\text{Neural Inference}} + \underbrace{t_{\text{cbf}}}_{\text{Safety QP Filter}} + \underbrace{t_{\text{act}}}_{\text{Inverter \& Coil Rise}} \le \frac{1}{f_{\text{ctrl}}}$$

::: {tbl-colwidths="[12,18,12,58]"}

| **Symbol**             | **Definition**                     | **Unit**    | **Notes**                                                                                                                          |
|:-----------------------|:-----------------------------------|:------------|:-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **$T_{\text{loop}}$**  | **Total Closed-Loop Latency**      | $\text{ms}$ | End-to-end wall-clock time from photon arrival/sensor sampling to mechanical torque realization.                                   |
| **$t_{\text{sense}}$** | **Sensor Integration Time**        | $\text{ms}$ | Physical exposure duration, ADC conversion, and sensor pipeline readout latency.                                                   |
| **$t_{\text{xfer}}$**  | **Interconnect Transfer Time**     | $\text{ms}$ | DMA bus streaming, PCIe handoff, and serializer deserializer (SerDes) link latency.                                                |
| **$t_{\text{infer}}$** | **Neural Policy Inference Time**   | $\text{ms}$ | Forward-pass compute time of the cognitive vision-language-action (VLA) or policy network.                                         |
| **$t_{\text{cbf}}$**   | **Control Barrier Filter Latency** | $\text{ms}$ | Execution time of the deterministic Quadratic Program (QP) solving the barrier safety projection.                                  |
| **$t_{\text{act}}$**   | **Actuator Electrical Rise Time**  | $\text{ms}$ | Gate driver PWM modulation, phase current rise time ($L/R$ time constant), and field buildup.                                      |
| **$f_{\text{ctrl}}$**  | **Control Execution Frequency**    | $\text{Hz}$ | Target closed-loop execution rate (e.g., $1000\text{ Hz}$ for joint reflex loops; $20\text{--}50\text{ Hz}$ for cognitive chunks). |

:::

## The Action-Chunking Streaming Cadence Law {#sec-notation-chunking-cadence .unlisted}

Cognitive neural policies cannot execute at kilohertz frequencies due to memory bandwidth limits. Action chunking predicts an action trajectory of horizon $H$ at a lower cognitive frequency $f_{\text{policy}}$, while real-time reflexes execute at $f_{\text{ctrl}}$. The memory streaming latency must remain bounded by the chunk execution window:

$$t_{\text{stream}} = \frac{M_{\text{weights}}}{\text{BW}_{\text{mem}}} \le \frac{H}{f_{\text{exec}}} - t_{\text{compute}}$$

::: {tbl-colwidths="[12,18,12,58]"}

| **Symbol**                   | **Definition**                 | **Unit**    | **Notes**                                                                                                    |
|:-----------------------------|:-------------------------------|:------------|:-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **$H$**                      | **Action Chunk Horizon**       | Time steps  | Number of contiguous future action steps generated in a single policy forward pass (e.g., $H=16$ or $H=32$). |
| **$M_{\text{weights}}$**     | **Model Parameter Footprint**  | bytes       | Total memory required to store policy weights ($P \times \text{bytes-per-parameter}$).                       |
| **$\text{BW}_{\text{mem}}$** | **Sustained Memory Bandwidth** | bytes/s     | Achievable memory throughput of the SoC or accelerator memory subsystem (e.g., LPDDR5, HBM).                 |
| **$t_{\text{stream}}$**      | **Parameter Streaming Time**   | $\text{ms}$ | Time required to stream non-resident model weights into execution registers.                                 |
| **$f_{\text{exec}}$**        | **Action Execution Rate**      | $\text{Hz}$ | Temporal consumption rate of chunked waypoints along the planned trajectory ($100\text{--}1000\text{ Hz}$).  |

:::

## The Dynamic Stopping and Safety Invariants {#sec-notation-stopping-invariant .unlisted}

Forward-invariance of safe set $\mathcal{C}$ dictates that the machine must maintain sufficient braking distance to arrest all motion before violating environmental boundary $d_{\text{gap}}$:

$$d_{\text{stop}}(v) = \underbrace{v \cdot t_{\text{react}}}_{\text{Reaction Distance}} + \underbrace{\frac{v^2}{2 a_{\max}}}_{\text{Deceleration Distance}} + \underbrace{\frac{v^3}{6 j_{\max}}}_{\text{Jerk Ramp Distance}} \le d_{\text{gap}}$$

::: {tbl-colwidths="[12,18,12,58]"}

| **Symbol**             | **Definition**              | **Unit**       | **Notes**                                                                                                   |
|:-----------------------|:----------------------------|:---------------|:------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **$d_{\text{stop}}$**  | **Total Stopping Envelope** | $\text{m}$     | Minimum distance required to bring the physical plant to a complete halt from velocity $v$.                 |
| **$d_{\text{gap}}$**   | **Clearance Margin**        | $\text{m}$     | Distance from the current machine position to the nearest obstacle or kinematic boundary.                   |
| **$t_{\text{react}}$** | **System Reaction Time**    | $\text{s}$     | Combined sensor stall detection latency, intent lease expiry, and brake engagement time.                    |
| **$v_{\max}, v$**      | **Velocity Limits**         | $\text{m/s}$   | Maximum allowable operational velocity and instantaneous state velocity.                                    |
| **$a_{\max}$**         | **Maximum Deceleration**    | $\text{m/s}^2$ | Peak actuator or braking deceleration capability within plant thermal and structural limits.                |
| **$j_{\max}$**         | **Jerk Limit**              | $\text{m/s}^3$ | Maximum rate of change of deceleration, bounded to prevent mechanical gearbox shock and drivetrain ringing. |

:::

## 1. Physical Plant State, Dynamics, and Actuation

::: {tbl-colwidths="[12,18,12,58]"}

| **Symbol**                                     | **Definition**                | **Unit**                                 | **Notes**                                                                                                                                      |
|:-----------------------------------------------|:------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **$s_t \in \mathcal{S}$**                      | **Physical World State**      | Mixed                                    | Ground-truth continuous state of the machine, environment, and physical contacts at time $t$.                                                  |
| **$\mathbf{x}$**                               | **Mechanical Plant State**    | $\text{rad, rad/s}$                      | Generalized state vector $\mathbf{x} = [\mathbf{q}^\top, \dot{\mathbf{q}}^\top]^\top \in \mathbb{R}^{2n}$ containing positions and velocities. |
| **$o_t \in \mathcal{O}$**                      | **Sensor Observation**        | Mixed                                    | Digital sensor telemetry (images, depth maps, joint encoders, tactile arrays, IMU).                                                            |
| **$a_t \in \mathcal{A}$**                      | **Cognitive Policy Action**   | Normalized                               | Raw unprivileged action emitted by neural policy $\pi_\theta$.                                                                                 |
| **$\hat{u}_t$**                                | **Proposed Control Setpoint** | $\text{N}\cdot\text{m}$ / $\text{rad}$   | Downsampled or unprivileged control candidate submitted across the causal boundary.                                                            |
| **$u^*_t$**                                    | **Certified Control Action**  | $\text{N}\cdot\text{m}$ / $\text{rad}$   | Privileged, safety-filtered control command emitted by the real-time CBF-QP filter.                                                            |
| **$\mathbf{q} \in \mathbb{R}^n$**              | **Joint Coordinate Vector**   | $\text{rad}$ or $\text{m}$               | Generalized coordinates describing the mechanical articulation of $n$ degrees of freedom.                                                      |
| **$\dot{\mathbf{q}} \in \mathbb{R}^n$**        | **Joint Velocity Vector**     | $\text{rad/s}$ or $\text{m/s}$           | Time derivative of generalized joint coordinates.                                                                                              |
| **$\ddot{\mathbf{q}} \in \mathbb{R}^n$**       | **Joint Acceleration Vector** | $\text{rad/s}^2$ or $\text{m/s}^2$       | Second time derivative of generalized coordinates.                                                                                             |
| **$\boldsymbol{\tau} \in \mathbb{R}^n$**       | **Actuator Torque Vector**    | $\text{N}\cdot\text{m}$ or $\text{N}$    | Generalized forces and torques delivered by actuators at mechanical joints.                                                                    |
| **$\mathbf{M}(\mathbf{q})$**                   | **Inertia Matrix**            | $\text{kg}\cdot\text{m}^2$               | Symmetric positive-definite generalized mass/inertia matrix of the articulated multibody plant.                                                |
| **$\mathbf{C}(\mathbf{q}, \dot{\mathbf{q}})$** | **Coriolis Matrix**           | $\text{N}\cdot\text{m}\cdot\text{s/rad}$ | Matrix of Coriolis and centrifugal generalized forces.                                                                                         |
| **$\mathbf{g}(\mathbf{q})$**                   | **Gravity Vector**            | $\text{N}\cdot\text{m}$                  | Generalized gravitational forces acting on links as a function of configuration.                                                               |
| **$\mathbf{J}(\mathbf{q})$**                   | **Manipulator Jacobian**      | Mixed                                    | Linear mapping from joint velocities $\dot{\mathbf{q}}$ to operational task-space velocity $\mathbf{v}_e = \mathbf{J}\dot{\mathbf{q}}$.        |
| **$N_{\text{gear}}$**                          | **Gear Reduction Ratio**      | Dimensionless                            | Transmission reduction ratio ($N_{\text{gear}} \gg 1$) between motor rotor and joint output.                                                   |
| **$N_{\text{gear}}^2 J_{\text{rotor}}$**       | **Reflected Rotor Inertia**   | $\text{kg}\cdot\text{m}^2$               | Apparent rotor inertia amplified quadratically by gearbox reduction ratio.                                                                     |
| **$\eta_{\text{gear}}$**                       | **Transmission Efficiency**   | Dimensionless                            | Mechanical power transmission efficiency ($0 < \eta_{\text{gear}} \le 1$).                                                                     |

:::

## 2. Geometry, Frames, and Spatial Transformations

::: {tbl-colwidths="[12,18,12,58]"}

| **Symbol**                                    | **Definition**               | **Unit**      | **Notes**                                                                                                                     |
|:----------------------------------------------|:-----------------------------|:--------------|:------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **$SE(3)$**                                   | **Special Euclidean Group**  | Lie Group     | Lie group of rigid-body transformations (translations and rotations in 3D: $\mathbb{R}^3 \times SO(3)$).                      |
| **$SO(3)$**                                   | **Special Orthogonal Group** | Lie Group     | Group of $3 \times 3$ proper orthogonal rotation matrices ($\mathbf{R}^\top \mathbf{R} = \mathbf{I}, \det(\mathbf{R}) = +1$). |
| **$\mathcal{F}_W, \mathcal{F}_B$**            | **Coordinate Frames**        | Reference     | Fixed World reference frame ($\mathcal{F}_W$) and robot Body/base reference frame ($\mathcal{F}_B$).                          |
| **$\mathbf{p} \in \mathbb{R}^3$**             | **Cartesian Position**       | $\text{m}$    | Translation coordinates $[x, y, z]^\top$ relative to a specified reference frame.                                             |
| **$\mathbf{R} \in SO(3)$**                    | **Rotation Matrix**          | Dimensionless | $3 \times 3$ directional cosine matrix representing spatial orientation.                                                      |
| **$\mathbf{q}_{\text{quat}} \in \mathbb{H}$** | **Unit Quaternion**          | Dimensionless | Unit quaternion $[w, x, y, z]^\top$ representing 3D orientation ($\lVert \mathbf{q}_{\text{quat}} \rVert = 1$).               |
| **$\mathbf{T}_{A \to B}$**                    | **Homogeneous Transform**    | Dimensionless | $4 \times 4$ rigid transform matrix mapping homogeneous coordinates from frame $A$ to frame $B$.                              |
| **$\mathbf{Ad}_T$**                           | **Adjoint Representation**   | Matrix        | $6 \times 6$ matrix mapping spatial twists and wrenches between coordinate frames.                                            |
| **$\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{\text{depth}}$**      | **Depth Spatial Covariance** | $\text{m}^2$  | 3D uncertainty ellipsoidal covariance matrix associated with perception depth lifting.                                        |

:::

## 3. Cognitive Deliberation, Chunking, and Data Flywheels

::: {tbl-colwidths="[12,18,12,58]"}

| **Symbol**                        | **Definition**                  | **Unit**            | **Notes**                                                                                                   |
|:----------------------------------|:--------------------------------|:--------------------|:------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **$\pi_\theta(a \mid o)$**        | **Parameterized Policy**        | Probability density | Neural network policy parameterized by weights $\theta$, mapping observations to action distributions.      |
| **$\mathbf{z} \in \mathbb{R}^d$** | **Latent Representation**       | Dimensionless       | Compressed spatial-semantic feature embedding extracted by perception encoders.                             |
| **$\mathbf{A}_{t:t+H}$**          | **Action Chunk Trajectory**     | Sequence            | contiguous sequence of $H$ future action predictions $[a_t, a_{t+1}, \dots, a_{t+H-1}]$.                    |
| **$\mathcal{D}_{\text{demo}}$**   | **Nominal Demonstration Data**  | Trajectories        | Dataset of nominal expert demonstrations used for behavioral cloning.                                       |
| **$\mathcal{D}_{\text{rec}}$**    | **Recovery Intervention Data**  | Trajectories        | Dataset of human takeovers, corrections, and recovery maneuvers from boundary states.                       |
| **$\epsilon_{\text{BC}}$**        | **Single-Step Imitation Error** | Dimensionless       | Probability of single-step error under policy rollouts ($\epsilon_{\text{BC}} \in [0, 1]$).                 |
| **$O(T^2 \epsilon)$**             | **Compounding Covariate Drift** | Error bound         | Quadratic compounding drift under uncorrected open-loop rollout trajectories of duration $T$.               |
| **$\Lambda_{\text{intent}}$**     | **Expiring Intent Lease**       | Contract            | Cryptographically signed, bounded time-to-live execution permit granted to neural policies.                 |
| **$T_{\text{lease}}$**            | **Intent Lease Duration**       | $\text{ms}$         | Maximum duration of autonomous execution authority before mandatory re-certification ($\le 100\text{ ms}$). |

:::

## 4. Real-Time Safety Enforcement and Authority Handshakes

::: {tbl-colwidths="[12,18,12,58]"}

| **Symbol**                            | **Definition**                        | **Unit**        | **Notes**                                                                                                  |
|:--------------------------------------|:--------------------------------------|:----------------|:-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **$\mathcal{C} \subset \mathcal{S}$** | **Safe Operating Set**                | Set             | Forward-invariant set where safety invariants and physical constraints are satisfied.                      |
| **$\partial \mathcal{C}$**            | **Safety Set Boundary**               | Boundary        | Zero superlevel set defined by $h(\mathbf{x}) = 0$.                                                        |
| **$h(\mathbf{x}) \ge 0$**             | **Control Barrier Function**          | Real scalar     | Continuously differentiable function whose superlevel set defines forward-invariant set $\mathcal{C}$.     |
| **$L_{\mathbf{f}} h(\mathbf{x})$**    | **Lie Derivative along Drift**        | $\text{s}^{-1}$ | Directional derivative of scalar barrier $h(\mathbf{x})$ along plant drift field $\mathbf{f}(\mathbf{x})$. |
| **$L_{\mathbf{g}} h(\mathbf{x})$**    | **Lie Derivative along Control**      | Real vector     | Gradient of barrier $h(\mathbf{x})$ projected along control input field $\mathbf{g}(\mathbf{x})$.          |
| **$\gamma_{\text{cbf}}$**             | **Class-$\mathcal{K}$ Barrier Decay** | $\text{s}^{-1}$ | Extended class-$\mathcal{K}$ linear decay coefficient in barrier inequality $\dot{h} + \gamma h \ge 0$.    |
| **$\alpha(t)$**                       | **Bumpless Transfer Blending**        | $[0, 1]$        | $C^2$-continuous quintic transition coefficient ramping between autonomous and manual control.             |
| **$\mathcal{T}_{\text{trichotomy}}$** | **Trichotomy Decision State**         | Enum            | Three-valued monitor classification: $\{\text{Known-True}, \text{Known-False}, \text{Unknown}\}$.          |

:::

## 5. Embedded Silicon, Thermal Dissipation, and Electrical Limits

::: {tbl-colwidths="[12,18,12,58]"}

| **Symbol**                    | **Definition**                    | **Unit**                        | **Notes**                                                                                                                                            |
|:------------------------------|:----------------------------------|:--------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **$I_{\text{phase}}$**        | **Motor Phase Current**           | $\text{Amperes (A)}$            | RMS electrical current driving stator windings in brushless permanent magnet motors.                                                                 |
| **$R_{\text{phase}}$**        | **Phase Winding Resistance**      | $\text{Ohms } (\Omega)$         | DC electrical resistance of stator coil windings.                                                                                                    |
| **$C_{\text{th}}$**           | **Stator Thermal Capacitance**    | $\text{J/K}$                    | Lumped thermal capacitance of the actuator stator core and potting compound.                                                                         |
| **$\Delta T$**                | **Joulean Stator Thermal Rise**   | $\text{Kelvin (K)}$             | Temperature rise under sustained electrical load ($\Delta T = I^2 R \Delta t / C_{\text{th}}$).                                                      |
| **$L_{\text{bus}}$**          | **Power Distribution Inductance** | $\text{Henries } (\mu\text{H})$ | Parasitic harness and PCB track inductance supplying power inverters.                                                                                |
| **$\Delta V_{\text{droop}}$** | **Dynamic Rail Voltage Droop**    | $\text{Volts (V)}$              | Transient voltage collapse ($L_{\text{bus}} \frac{\mathrm{d}I}{\mathrm{d}t} + I R_{\text{bus}}$) triggered by sudden compute or inverter step loads. |
| **$\Delta t_{\text{fresh}}$** | **Telemetry Freshness Deadline**  | $\text{ms}$                     | Maximum allowable age of sensor telemetry before an interlock is triggered.                                                                          |
| **$t_{\text{NMI}}$**          | **Non-Maskable Interrupt Time**   | $\mu\text{s}$                   | Deterministic hardware interrupt response time for stale-heartbeat or over-current detection.                                                        |

:::
